sentences.text: The single known species, M. laurillardi, reached a length exceeding 4 meters.
The genus Mystriosaurus was first described by Kaup in 1834, with M. laurillardi serving as its type species.
Fossil specimens have been found in Germany, specifically within the Posidonia Shale, and in the Whitby Mudstone of England.
Scientists have recorded 31 fossil occurrences of this animal in the Paleobiology Database.
This animal belongs to the family Teleosauridae and is classified within the suborder Thalattosuchia.
Steneosaurus brevior was once considered a synonym of Mystriosaurus, but a 2019 phylogenetic analysis determined that Mystriosaurus is distinct from the genus Steneosaurus.
Mystriosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Toarcian age, with fossils dating from the Hettangian to the Toarcian between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
